standard_prerequisites.name: Cardinal numbers and cardinal inequality
standard_prerequisites.statement: card is the set-truncation of the type of sets; alpha<=beta means there is an injection from a representative of alpha to a representative of beta.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the relation the statement is about, and the proof reasons on representatives.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cantor's theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a set A there is no surjection A -> (A->bool).
standard_prerequisites.use: The second half of the proof contradicts it.

standard_prerequisites.name: Injections versus surjections
standard_prerequisites.statement: Lemma 10.2.9: under excluded middle an injection A->B into an inhabited B yields a surjection A->B.
standard_prerequisites.use: It turns the assumed injection (A->bool) -> A into a surjection, which Cantor's theorem forbids.

core_obligations: Take beta = 2^alpha and show alpha <= beta: reduce the mere proposition to representatives, so that beta is cd{A->bool}, and build the explicit injection f(a)(a') = true when a=a' and false otherwise, using excluded middle (source lines 871-881).

Show alpha is different from beta: if 2^alpha <= alpha there is an injection (A->bool)->A, and since the function constantly false inhabits A->bool, Lemma 10.2.9 turns that injection into a surjection A->(A->bool), contradicting Cantor's theorem (source lines 883-884).

proof_roadmap.step: Construct the diagonal injection A->(A->bool) using decidable equality and read off alpha<=2^alpha.
Assume 2^alpha<=alpha, convert the injection into a surjection via the lemma on injections, and contradict Cantor's theorem.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled corollary at source lines 867-869, original Corollary 10.2.13: assuming excluded middle, for every cardinal alpha there is a cardinal beta with alpha<=beta and alpha not equal to beta. Its identity is its position in the first-edition numbering, since the author gave it no label; it sits in section 10.2 immediately after Cantor's theorem. The proof (source lines 870-885) has two halves of different character: the first builds an explicit injection A->(A->bool) by deciding a=a' for each pair, and must first discharge the set-truncation of card so that the reasoning can be done on a representative A; the second assumes the opposite inequality, converts an injection into a surjection through the preceding lemma on injections, and has to notice that the constantly-false function inhabits the target, which is what makes that lemma applicable.
